data.name: Barbados
data.summary: Barbados has no capital gains, inheritance, gift or wealth tax, but it does tax resident and domiciled individuals on worldwide income at 11.5% up to BBD 50,000 and 27.5% above (2026). Local dividends bear a 15% final withholding tax; foreign dividends are taxed at the marginal rate with a foreign tax credit. Resident but non-domiciled individuals are taxed on foreign income only to the extent a benefit is obtained in Barbados. Real estate and private-company share transfers bear 2.5% property transfer tax plus 1% stamp duty. Treaty network of 30-40 countries, including the US and UK.

regimes.name: Resident and domiciled
regimes.description: Worldwide income taxation for individuals resident and domiciled in Barbados.
regimes.eligibility: Resident (more than 182 days in a calendar year, or ordinarily resident) and domiciled in Barbados.

capital_gains.important_exceptions: Property transfer tax 2.5% on the value of land with buildings above BBD 150,000 (on the whole value of land without buildings) and on private-company shares above BBD 50,000, plus stamp duty BBD 10 per BBD 1,000 (1%). Listed shares on the Barbados Stock Exchange are exempt. Gains from trading are taxed as business income at income tax rates; there are no specific capital gains rules.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Barbados does not impose capital gains tax (PwC Oct 2026; Deloitte 2026; Invest Barbados).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains of a trade (e.g. frequent dealing) are business income taxed at 11.5%/27.5%.

dividends.summary: Resident and domiciled individuals: dividends from Barbados companies bear a 15% final withholding tax; foreign dividends are taxed at ordinary income tax rates (11.5% up to BBD 50,000, 27.5% above, for 2026) with credit for foreign tax, limited so Barbados tax is not reduced below 1% of taxable income.
dividends.important_exceptions: A 2% foreign exchange fee applies to transactions requiring remittance or settlement in foreign currency unless made from a foreign currency account.

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 15% final WHT on dividends from post-June 1992 profits. Foreign: top marginal rate 27.5% (income year 2026, PwC Oct 2026; Deloitte Jan 2026 still shows 28.5%).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Dividends to non-residents: 0% if paid out of foreign-source income, otherwise 5% (non-treaty); treaty rates 0-15%.
dividends.treaty_network: About 33 treaties listed by PwC (29 in force) incl. US (5/15), UK (0/15), Canada (15), Switzerland, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Italy, Portugal, CARICOM; Deloitte cites more than 40 jurisdictions incl. CARICOM. The US treaty reduces US WHT on portfolio dividends to 15%.

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax, but gifts may be subject to property transfer tax (2.5%) and stamp duty (1%) on real estate and private-company shares (Deloitte 2026).
inheritance.domicile_rules: No transfer taxes, so domicile is irrelevant for them.

regimes.name: Resident but not domiciled
regimes.description: Individuals resident but not domiciled in Barbados are taxed on Barbados-source income and on foreign-source income only to the extent a benefit is obtained in Barbados (a remittance-type basis).
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident but domiciled elsewhere (common-law domicile; a newly arrived foreign family normally keeps its domicile of origin). No time limit found.
regimes.duration_note: No statutory time limit: the Income Tax Act taxes a resident but non-domiciled individual on Barbados income and on foreign income only to the extent a benefit is obtained in Barbados (PwC, Individual - Taxes on personal income, reviewed 9 Oct 2026), and neither PwC nor Deloitte reports a deemed-domicile or year-count rule. The status lasts while the individual keeps a foreign domicile under common law; it ends if the individual acquires a Barbados domicile of choice (settling in Barbados with the intention of staying permanently), which is a question of fact that a long-settled family may eventually face.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends kept and used outside Barbados are not taxed; amounts from which a benefit is obtained in Barbados are taxed at up to 27.5%. Local dividends: 15% final WHT.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Resident but not domiciled in Barbados. The 0% rate on foreign dividends assumes that no benefit from them is obtained in Barbados, i.e. the dividends (and capital derived from them) are kept and spent abroad and not remitted to or enjoyed in Barbados. Any foreign dividends from which a benefit is obtained in Barbados are taxed at the ordinary rates (11.5% to BBD 50,000, 27.5% above, 2026), with foreign tax credit.

income.name: Barbados

income_tax.summary: Two-band income tax after a BBD 25,000 personal allowance: 11.5% on the next BBD 50,000 and 27.5% above that, from income year 2026 (cut from 12.5% and 28.5%). National Insurance is 11% of earnings up to BBD 5,360 a month for employees and 17% for the self-employed.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay 17% of earnings to the National Insurance Scheme (PwC), on the same monthly ceiling of BBD 5,360. Both employees and self-employed also pay a further 0.25% of gross earnings, uncapped, to the Resilience and Regeneration Fund (formerly the Catastrophe Fund). Cap shown is BBD 5,360 x 12.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local or municipal income tax. Brackets are on taxable income after the BBD 25,000 personal allowance: the BRA describes the 11.5% band as gross income of BBD 25,001 to 75,000 and 27.5% above BBD 75,000. Residents who are not domiciled are taxed on Barbados-source income and on foreign income only to the extent a benefit is obtained in Barbados. The 0.25% Resilience and Regeneration Fund levy is not included in the employee rate shown.

regimes.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
regimes.description: 12-month remote-work visa for people working for employers or clients outside Barbados (fee USD 2,000 individual, USD 3,000 family; reapply after a year). The official programme page states: 'You will not be liable to pay Barbados Income Tax and therefore will not be subject to any double taxation'; the visa is for remote work only. Because the holder is expressly allowed to work remotely in Barbados and is told no Barbados income tax is payable, the relief covers pay for work done while living there (covers_local_work true); 17.5% VAT still applies to purchases.
regimes.duration_note: Valid 12 months; the tourism site says holders can 'easily reapply' but gives no renewal terms or fees, so 2 years assumes one reapplication. Fee USD 2,000 individual, USD 3,000 family bundle.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens use the same route for remote work: the 12-month Welcome Stamp (USD 50,000 a year of income from outside Barbados; USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family fee). Skilled employees of a Barbadian employer need a local work permit and a long-term residence status; the Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) is a separate high-net-worth/retiree route. Permit thresholds, fees and processing for employees were not verified on an official page. US citizens stay taxable in the US on worldwide income regardless of the Welcome Stamp exemption.
